text.p: The San Diego Padres re-signed veteran left-hander Fernando Valenzuela to a one-year contract Tuesday night, a day before they would have lost the right to negotiate with him until May.
The portly, 36-year-old left-hander was a pleasant surprise for the National League West champions last season, going 13-8 with a 3.62 ERA in 33 games, including 31 starts.
Valenzuela has compiled a 171-141 record with a 3.50 ERA in a 16-year career with Los Angeles, California, Baltimore, Philadelphia and San Diego.
Valenzuela became a free agent December 20th after rejecting the team's offer of salary arbitration. But he Tuesday night he said he feels good about returning to San Diego.
"Returning to the Padres was my first preference. I am excited about 1997 and will do my best for the team and the fans of San Diego," he said.

"We are thrilled to have a pitcher and person the calibre of Fernando Valenzuela in the Padres organisation," said Padres' president Larry Lucchino. "His experience, heart, leadership and performance are invaluable to this ballclub."
